description: Deployment configuration, backup scripts, and comprehensive README. Depends on FEAT-001 through FEAT-003. Independent of each other — could run in parallel with FEAT-003 but for safety runs after all code is complete.
steps: Step 1 — Create server/render.yaml: Render deployment manifest. Define a web service: name: oma-midas-api, env: node, region: oregon, plan: starter, buildCommand: 'npm install && npx prisma generate && npx prisma migrate deploy', startCommand: 'node server.js', healthCheckPath: /health. envVars list all required variables (PORT, DATABASE_URL, JWT_SECRET, JWT_EXPIRES_IN, PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY, PAYSTACK_PUBLIC_KEY, FRONTEND_URL, EMAIL_HOST, EMAIL_PORT, EMAIL_USER, EMAIL_PASS, EMAIL_FROM, NODE_ENV, SENTRY_DSN) each with generateValue or sync: false as appropriate.

Step 2 — Create client/vercel.json: {"rewrites":[{"source":"/(.*)","destination":"/index.html"}]}. This ensures React Router works on Vercel (all paths serve index.html). Also add build config: {"buildCommand":"npm run build","outputDirectory":"dist","installCommand":"npm install"}.

Step 3 — Create server/scripts/backup.js (ES module). Import child_process (execSync), path, fs, dotenv. Load .env. Build pg_dump command using DATABASE_URL env var. Output to backups/backup-YYYY-MM-DD-HH-mm.sql. Create backups/ dir if not exists. Run pg_dump. Log success with file path and size. Export runBackup() for cron use. Add npm script to server/package.json: 'backup': 'node scripts/backup.js'. Add a note at top of file explaining restore procedure: `psql DATABASE_URL < backup-file.sql`.

Step 4 — Create scripts/backup.cron.js: wraps the backup and adds a weekly cron: '0 2 * * 0' (Sundays at 2am). Exports startBackupCronJob(). Note: this is optional/separate from the main server — run independently or import in server.js conditionally when ENABLE_BACKUP_CRON=true.

Step 5 — Create the root README.md. Must include all of these sections:

  # Oma Midas Global Limited — Savings & Loan Cooperative Platform

  ## Project Overview
  Brief description of the platform, its purpose, the cooperative model (12-month cycles, savings + loan fund), and the two portals (member + admin).

  ## Architecture
  Diagram (ASCII art) showing: Browser → Vercel (React SPA) → Render (Express API) → Supabase (Postgres). Paystack APIs ↔ Express. Nodemailer → SMTP.

  ## Prerequisites
  Node.js 18+, npm 9+, PostgreSQL client (for pg_dump), Supabase account, Paystack account, SMTP email account.

  ## Local Development Setup
  Step-by-step:
  1. Clone repo
  2. `cd server && npm install`
  3. Copy server/.env.example to server/.env and fill all values
  4. `npx prisma migrate dev` — runs migrations
  5. `node src/prisma/seed.js` — seeds admin account and settings
  6. `npm run dev` — starts backend on port 5000
  7. In a new terminal: `cd client && npm install`
  8. Copy client/.env.example to client/.env and fill values
  9. `npm run dev` — starts frontend on port 5173

  ## Default Admin Credentials
  Email: admin@omamidas.com | Password: Admin@Midas2024! (CHANGE IN PRODUCTION)

  ## Environment Variables Reference
  Table with Variable, Description, Example for every env var in both .env.example files.

  ## Paystack Configuration
  - Webhook URL: https://your-backend-domain.onrender.com/api/paystack/webhook
  - Add to Paystack dashboard: Settings → API Keys & Webhooks → Webhook URL
  - Events to enable: charge.success, transfer.success, transfer.failed, transfer.reversed
  - Test payment instructions: use Paystack test card 4084 0840 8408 4081 with any future expiry and CVV 408
  - Test bank transfer: use Paystack test bank details from their docs

  ## Deployment Guide
  ### Backend (Render)
  1. Push code to GitHub
  2. Create Render web service, connect repo, set root dir to server/
  3. Set all env vars in Render dashboard
  4. Render uses render.yaml for build/start commands
  5. After first deploy: verify /health endpoint returns 200

  ### Frontend (Vercel)
  1. Import repo to Vercel, set root dir to client/
  2. Set VITE_API_URL=https://your-backend.onrender.com/api
  3. Set VITE_PAYSTACK_PUBLIC_KEY=pk_live_...
  4. Deploy — Vercel auto-detects Vite

  ### Database (Supabase)
  1. Create Supabase project
  2. Get connection string (Transaction mode, port 6543 for pooling)
  3. Set as DATABASE_URL in server/.env and Render env vars
  4. Run `npx prisma migrate deploy` on first deploy

  ## Go-Live Checklist
  - [ ] All env vars set in Render and Vercel dashboards
  - [ ] Paystack webhook URL registered and verified
  - [ ] Paystack live keys configured (replace test keys)
  - [ ] Admin password changed from default
  - [ ] SMTP credentials verified (test send email)
  - [ ] Supabase connection string uses correct pooling mode
  - [ ] CORS set to production frontend URL only
  - [ ] JWT_SECRET is a strong random secret (32+ chars)
  - [ ] NODE_ENV=production on server
  - [ ] /health endpoint returns 200
  - [ ] Database migrations applied (`npx prisma migrate deploy`)
  - [ ] Seed script run (admin account created)
  - [ ] Active cycle created for current year (Oct 1 - Sep 30)
  - [ ] Sentry DSN configured for error monitoring (optional)

  ## Backup & Restore
  ### Create a backup:
  ```bash
  cd server && node scripts/backup.js
  ```
  Backup files are saved to server/backups/ as SQL dumps.

  ### Schedule automatic weekly backups:
  Set ENABLE_BACKUP_CRON=true in server .env to run weekly backup cron.

  ### Restore from backup:
  ```bash
  psql YOUR_DATABASE_URL < server/backups/backup-YYYY-MM-DD-HH-mm.sql
  ```
  WARNING: This will overwrite all data in the target database.

  ## Security Notes
  - JWT tokens stored in httpOnly cookies (not localStorage)
  - CORS restricted to FRONTEND_URL only
  - All admin routes verify ADMIN role server-side
  - Paystack webhooks verified with HMAC-SHA512
  - Rate limiting on all auth endpoints (10 req/15min)
  - Input validation with Zod on all endpoints
  - Passwords hashed with bcrypt (cost factor 12)
  - Never log secrets, JWTs, or full card/bank details

  ## Money Handling
  All monetary values stored and calculated in kobo (1 NGN = 100 kobo) as integers. Never use floats for money. The kobo.js utility provides safe conversion functions.

  ## Cooperative Business Rules
  - Cycles: October 1 to September 30 each year
  - Monthly contribution: set in settings (monthly_contribution_kobo)
  - Loan eligibility: 3+ consecutive paid months (NEW members), immediate (EXISTING members)
  - Loan maximum: 3x total savings in current cycle
  - Loan fee: 30% of requested amount (stays in company fund)
  - Member receives: 70% of requested amount
  - Total repayable: 100% of requested amount (no extra interest beyond fee)
  - Refunds blocked if any outstanding loan balance

  ## Contributing
  Internal project — contact project maintainer for access.
